newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader sees end to war by year's end.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader sees end to war by year's end.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga said on Wednesday a more professional approach to the war against Tamil Tiger rebels and a plan offering autonomy to minority Tamils could bring peace by year's end.
"We're confident of achieving peace by the end of this year because our approach to the war is totally different from the previous regime's," she said in an interview on state television.

She said her People's Alliance government, which won power in 1994, had given the military proper direction and all the arms and equipment they required to fight Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
"We've won victories which could not have been thought of in the past," she said, referring to the military's campaign which ousted Tamil rebels from their northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold.
"The armed forces have liberated three-fourths of the north which earlier was totally under LTTE control," she said. "The rest can be brought under control soon."
But she said the ethnic problem could not be solved merely by winning the war against Tamil rebels, who are fighting for a separate state in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
"The war cannot be ended without a fair and just solution to the ethnic problem," she said.
Kumaratunga said her peace plan offering extensive autonomy to minority Tamils was more generous than solutions proposed by previous regimes.
"A large section of the Tamil community is now against LTTE terrorists," she said. "A political solution is essential for peace. Tamil people are now moving away from the LTTE."
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year.
